comments.note: MEDIUM — A04 (Insecure Design) / A05 (Security Misconfiguration): CSP at server.ts line 105 uses 'unsafe-inline' for both script-src and style-src: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ...". This weakens XSS protection by allowing arbitrary inline script execution — a successful XSS injection could bypass the CSP entirely. This is an acknowledged, intentional trade-off for the current GUI architecture (inline scripts/styles). Does not block this WP. Recommended future remediation: migrate GUI scripts/styles to external files and replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonce- or hash-based CSP directives.

LOW — A05 (Security Misconfiguration): The last-resort .catch() 500 handler in main() (server.ts line 618) correctly includes securityHeaders() but omits corsHeaders(port). This is the only response path missing CORS headers. Not a security header gap (all 4 required headers are present), but a minor inconsistency. Recommended: add ...corsHeaders(port) to the last-resort handler for consistency with all other response paths.

A01 (Broken Access Control): Path traversal protection in serveStatic() (server.ts lines 420–423) uses Node's resolve() followed by a startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR) check — correct and robust pattern. No bypass vectors identified.

No security findings at Critical or High severity — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. securityHeaders() helper is implemented correctly: pure function returning a fresh object on each call (no shared mutable state), applied consistently across all response paths (sendJson, serveStatic, OPTIONS handler, last-resort 500 catch). Security sign-off: PASS.
